findings.title: Recovery-code JSON is written to the wrong UserCredentialModel field
findings.body: `createRecoveryCodesCredential` creates the federated credential input with `new UserCredentialModel("", credentialModel.getType(), recoveryCodesJson)`. The three-argument `UserCredentialModel` constructor populates `value`, not `challengeResponse`. The new user-storage implementation reads `input.getChallengeResponse()` when saving the recovery credential (`BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.updateCredential`), so the serialized code list is lost and `credentialData` is null. On the next login, `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` asks the storage for credentials and `BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials` attempts to deserialize that null data, so the user-storage recovery-code setup/login path fails. Use `setChallengeResponse` or make the storage read `getValue()`.

findings.title: Exhausted recovery credentials in user storage are not removed
findings.body: `RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential` now returns a credential from federated user storage when present, but the exhausted-code cleanup still calls `removeStoredCredentialById`, which is the local credential-store API. If all codes in a user-storage credential are used, the external credential remains configured. The next login will still select the recovery authenticator, but `RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean` calls `getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get()` on a credential with no remaining codes and throws, instead of redirecting the user to configure new codes. The removal/disable path must handle federated credentials.

findings.title: New user-storage test stores recovery codes in plaintext and permits replay
findings.body: The new user-storage handler stores the recovery-code payload verbatim in `credentialData`, and `isValid` at line 340 compares the submitted code to the raw stored strings. It never hashes incoming codes or marks a code as used. The production recovery-code provider stores hashes and consumes used codes. As written, the integration test models a storage backend that persists password-equivalent recovery codes in plaintext and accepts replay, and it would not catch a real user-storage implementation that fails to hash or consume codes.
